narrative:
The model estimates an 80% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically lead to employees departing.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and whether you have received other job offers. 

Your 6–10 years of total experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter experience (50% have only 1–5 years), the model sees mid-level experience like yours as a point where people often begin exploring new opportunities. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in your current organization also increased the likelihood of departure. This tenure is actually the most common range among those expected to stay, yet in your specific combination of circumstances it still contributed to the “will leave” direction.

Finally, the fact that you have received other job opportunities outside the company was another clear signal pulling the prediction toward leaving. Most employees the model expects to stay (77%) have not received such offers.

Taken together, these elements suggest you are at a career stage and in a situation where external options become attractive. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly and explore whether adjustments in responsibility, growth opportunities, or workload could increase your sense of stability and commitment. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel like the right long-term choice.
